mergePdf.name: Merge PDF
mergePdf.subtitle: Combine multiple PDFs into one file. Preserves Bookmarks.

mergePdf.retainPageLabelsHint: Off (default): the merged PDF uses natural page numbering 1–N. On: each file's original page labels are preserved (may produce duplicate labels).
mergePdf.faqCountQuestion: How many PDFs can I merge at once?
mergePdf.faqCountAnswer: Unlimited! Merge as many PDF files as you need in a single operation. No restrictions on file count or total size.
mergePdf.faqQualityAnswer: No! PagodaPDF preserves the original quality of all PDFs when merging. Your documents remain crisp and clear with no quality loss.
mergePdf.faqReorderQuestion: Can I reorder pages after selecting files?
mergePdf.faqReorderAnswer: Yes! Simply drag and drop files to arrange them in any order before clicking the merge button.

splitPdf.name: Split PDF
splitPdf.subtitle: Extract a range of pages into a new PDF.
splitPdf.modeAll: Split All Pages into Separate Files
splitPdf.faqRangeQuestion: Can I extract specific page ranges?
splitPdf.faqRangeAnswer: Yes! You can extract any specific pages or page ranges from your PDF. Select exactly which pages you need or split into individual files.
splitPdf.faqQualityAnswer: No! Split PDFs maintain the exact same quality as the original document. No compression or quality loss occurs.
splitPdf.faqBatchQuestion: Can I split multiple PDFs at once?
splitPdf.faqBatchAnswer: Yes, process multiple PDFs in batches for efficient document management.

compressPdf.faqAlgorithmQuestion: What's the difference between Condense and Photon?
compressPdf.faqAlgorithmAnswer: Condense removes unnecessary data, optimizes images, and subsets fonts. Photon converts pages to images, which is useful for scanned PDFs but makes text non-selectable.
compressPdf.faqLevelQuestion: Which compression level should I use?
compressPdf.faqLevelAnswer: Balanced offers strong size reduction with minimal quality loss. Use Light for maximum quality, Aggressive for smaller files, or Extreme for maximum compression.
compressPdf.faqLimitsAnswer: There are no fixed server upload limits because processing happens locally in your browser. Very large files are still limited by your device's available memory.

editPdfText.faqPrivacyAnswer: No. The whole editor — including the PDF engine — runs in your browser. Files are never uploaded anywhere.
editPdfText.faqLockedAnswer: Paragraphs using fragile subset fonts or complex layouts are protected so your document can't be silently corrupted. Everything else stays fully editable.
editPdfText.faqFontsQuestion: Will the fonts match the original?
editPdfText.faqFontsAnswer: Yes — the editor reuses the document's embedded fonts where possible, and you can also pull in fonts installed on your device.

duplexCollate.howItWorksStep1: Drop in the single PDF that holds all the front sides followed by all the back sides.

duplexCollate.faqOddPagesQuestion: What if my scan has an odd number of pages?
duplexCollate.faqOddPagesAnswer: A duplex scan should have an even page count. If it does not, a page was probably scanned twice or missed. The tool warns you before processing, and any unpaired pages are appended at the end so nothing is lost.
duplexCollate.faqBackOrderQuestion: Why would I keep the back block as-is?
duplexCollate.faqBackOrderAnswer: It depends on how the stack was fed for the second pass. Flipping the whole stack over produces back sides in reverse order, which is the default. If your scanner returned them in the same order as the fronts, choose to keep the block as-is.

digitalSignPdf.name: Digital Signature PDF
digitalSignPdf.pageTitle: Digital Signature PDF - Add Cryptographic Signature | PagodaPDF
digitalSignPdf.subtitle: Add a cryptographic digital signature to your PDF using X.509 certificates. Supports PKCS#12 (.pfx, .p12) and PEM formats. Your private key never leaves your browser.
digitalSignPdf.visibleSignatureDescription: When enabled, a visible signature box appears on the PDF. You can upload an image/logo or add text. If neither is provided, the signer's name from the certificate will be shown automatically.
digitalSignPdf.textPlaceholder: e.g., Digitally signed by John Doe

digitalSignPdf.missingDataMessage: Please upload both a PDF and a valid certificate.

digitalSignPdf.howToStep1Text: Select the PDF document you want to sign
digitalSignPdf.howToStep2Text: Provide your .pfx or .p12 certificate file and password
digitalSignPdf.howToStep3Text: Apply the digital signature and download your signed PDF
digitalSignPdf.faqWhatIsAnswer: A digital signature is a cryptographic mechanism that verifies the authenticity and integrity of a document. Unlike a drawn signature, it uses public key cryptography (X.509 certificates) to prove the signer's identity.
digitalSignPdf.faqFormatsAnswer: We support PKCS#12 format certificates (.pfx, .p12) which contain both your certificate and private key in a single encrypted file. These are commonly issued by certificate authorities.
digitalSignPdf.faqPrivateKeyAnswer: Yes! All processing happens entirely in your browser. Your certificate, private key, and PDF files never leave your device or get uploaded to any server.
digitalSignPdf.faqValidReadersQuestion: Will the signature be valid in PDF readers?
digitalSignPdf.faqValidReadersAnswer: Yes, the tool creates standard PKCS#7 detached signatures that are recognized by all major PDF viewers. For full validation, use a certificate from a trusted Certificate Authority.
digitalSignPdf.successMessage: PDF signed successfully! The signature can be verified in any PDF reader.
digitalSignPdf.internetRequiredDescription: Signing may need to fetch certificate chain information from your certificate issuer's server to validate the signature.
digitalSignPdf.invalidPositionMessage: Enter non-negative X and Y positions and a width and height greater than zero.

validateSignaturePdf.subtitle: Verify digital signatures in your PDF files. Check certificate validity, view signer details, and confirm document integrity. All processing happens in your browser.

validateSignaturePdf.trustVerification: Trust verification: {{verified}}/{{total}} signatures match the custom certificate chain
validateSignaturePdf.certificateExpired: Certificate expired or not yet valid
validateSignaturePdf.identityUnverified: Signature intact - signer identity not verified
validateSignaturePdf.howToStep1Text: Select the digitally signed PDF you want to inspect.
validateSignaturePdf.howToStep2Text: PagodaPDF checks each signature's cryptographic integrity and certificate.
validateSignaturePdf.howToStep3Text: Review signature coverage, certificate validity, and optional custom trust results.
validateSignaturePdf.faqTypesAnswer: The tool detects standard PDF PKCS#7 signatures that use X.509 certificates. Unsupported algorithms are clearly reported as unverified.
validateSignaturePdf.faqSelfSignedQuestion: What does a self-signed certificate mean?
validateSignaturePdf.faqSelfSignedAnswer: A self-signed certificate has not been vouched for by an external certificate authority. The signature integrity can still be checked, but the signer's identity is not automatically trusted.
validateSignaturePdf.faqPrivacyQuestion: Is my PDF uploaded to a server?
validateSignaturePdf.faqPrivacyAnswer: No. Signature analysis runs in your browser. A custom trust certificate also remains on your device.

timestampPdf.name: Timestamp PDF
timestampPdf.pageTitle: Timestamp PDF Online Free - RFC 3161 Document Timestamp | PagodaPDF
timestampPdf.subtitle: Add an RFC 3161 document timestamp to your PDF using a trusted Time Stamp Authority (TSA) server. Proves your document existed at a specific point in time. No certificate required.
timestampPdf.successMessage: PDF timestamped successfully! The timestamp can be verified in any PDF reader.
timestampPdf.internetRequiredDescription: Only a cryptographic hash of the document is sent to the selected TSA server to obtain a timestamp token.
timestampPdf.failureMessage: The timestamp could not be applied: {{message}} Try another TSA server or check your internet connection.
timestampPdf.howToStep1Text: Select the PDF document you want to timestamp.
timestampPdf.howToStep2Text: Select a trusted RFC 3161 Time Stamp Authority.
timestampPdf.howToStep3Text: Obtain the timestamp token and download the timestamped PDF.
timestampPdf.faqWhatAnswer: An RFC 3161 document timestamp is cryptographic proof that a document hash existed at a specific time. The signed token is embedded in the PDF.
timestampPdf.faqCertificateAnswer: No. The TSA signs the timestamp token with its own certificate.
timestampPdf.faqPrivacyQuestion: Is my document sent to the TSA server?
timestampPdf.faqPrivacyAnswer: No. Only a SHA-256 cryptographic hash is sent to the selected TSA server; the PDF itself remains on your device.
timestampPdf.faqReadersQuestion: Will PDF readers recognize the timestamp?
timestampPdf.faqReadersAnswer: The tool creates a standard RFC 3161 document timestamp recognized by major PDF readers.

pdfOverlay.faqDifferenceQuestion: What is the difference between overlay and underlay?
pdfOverlay.faqDifferenceAnswer: Overlay places pages on top of your base PDF (like a watermark). Underlay places pages behind your base PDF (like a letterhead or background).
pdfOverlay.faqSinglePageQuestion: Can I use a single-page PDF as overlay for all pages?
pdfOverlay.faqSinglePageAnswer: Yes! Enable the "Loop" option and your overlay PDF pages will repeat across all base pages. A single-page watermark will apply to every page.
pdfOverlay.faqPrivacyQuestion: Are my files private and secure?
pdfOverlay.faqPrivacyAnswer: Absolutely! All processing happens in your browser. Your files never leave your device, ensuring complete privacy.
